issues.description: The Bitmap24 class declaration in the template declares the image buffer member as 'int *data', but the implementation in Bitmap24.cpp allocates, uses and deletes it as a 'char' buffer (new char[...] / delete[] data). The solution repository's Bitmap24.hpp declares 'char *data'. This type mismatch is structural and will confuse students and can cause compilation/type issues when they implement or use the class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's Bitmap24.hpp declaration consistent with the implementation and solution by changing the member declaration from 'int *data;' to 'char *data;'. Alternatively, if int-array semantics are intended, update Bitmap24.cpp to allocate and manipulate an int buffer consistently. Prefer matching the solution and implementation: use 'char *data' and update any documentation/comment accordingly.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 class's data buffer member is declared with a different type in the template header compared to its usage in the implementation and the solution. In example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp (template) the member is declared as 'int *data;', but the implementation in example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp (template) allocates and treats it as a char buffer (new char[...], char pointer semantics). The solution's header declares the member as 'char *data;', matching the implementation. This mismatch of the 'data' attribute across header/implementation/solution creates a semantic inconsistency and an unnecessary cognitive/compilation burden for students trying to map the class interface to its implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template header with the implementation and solution by changing the Bitmap24::data declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'int *data;' to 'char *data;'. This makes the interface consistent with the implementation and with the solution reference.
